findings.title: upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) without null/missing handling
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py the new upsampled_count function is sum(Column(sample_weight)) wrapped in toInt64. Rows that were not client-sampled, old rows, or mixed transaction rows have no sample_weight (NULL/missing). SUM ignores NULLs so those events contribute 0 instead of 1, under-counting, and an all-NULL bucket returns NULL instead of 0. The helper even states no null checks are needed. Fix by using coalesce/ifNull e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1)) or equivalent.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py _get_event_stats takes scoped_dataset but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset. When the dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with a different split_dataset (discover vs scoped_dataset), the upsampling decision is made for the wrong dataset, so error splits may not be upsampled or transaction splits may be incorrectly upsampled.

findings.title: Cache key uses randomized Python hash() and caches global allowlist
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py the cache key is f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(...)))}". Python hash() for tuples is salted per-process and not stable across workers, so shared cache keys will miss/collide unpredictably and hash collisions can mix different project sets. Worse, the cached value is the global options.get allowlist result cached 60s, so allowlist changes are stale for up to 60s causing 10x over/under counts, and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere.

findings.title: Column transform only matches bare count()
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only transforms when column.lower().strip() == "count()". Any aliased form like "count() as foo", "count() AS count", equations, or count_unique/count_if variants pass through untransformed, so the endpoint silently mixes upsampled and raw counts depending on how the yAxis alias is spelled. The caller in organization_events_stats.py passes through final_columns verbatim, so this silently disables upsampling for those queries.

findings.title: Discover error detection only matches event.type:error
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py _is_error_focused_query returns True only if the substring "event.type:error" is in the query. Empty queries on the errors/discover path, negations like "!event.type:transaction", issue.category, event.type:default/csp/hprof, or error-only dashboard splits are treated as non-error, so allowlisted error queries are not upsampled (under-counted by sampling factor). Conversely errors-dataset queries are always upsampled regardless of query content.

findings.title: Sample-rate test helper swallows errors and drops falsy rates
findings.body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling uses bare try/except: pass around contexts lookup and float() conversion, and gates on if client_sample_rate: truthiness. A rate of 0, a numeric string edge case, or a malformed contexts shape is silently ignored, leaving sample_rate unset and making upsampling tests pass with weight 1 instead of failing loudly on bad fixture data.
